sentences.text: Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 01.03.2021.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (mother-in- law),
petitioner no. 4 and 5 (relatives), petitioner no. 6 and 7 (brother-in- law).

6. On 22.08.2023, parties arrived at a settlement before the Counselling Cell, Family Courts,
Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

entities.text:
Counselling Cell, Family Courts,
Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 4,50,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

The copy of the aforesaid settlement deed dated 22.08.2023 is on record (Annexure P-2).
7.
In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by divorce deed (talaqnama) dated 25.10.2023.

Further, as per the settlement, an amount of Rs. 2,50,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- has been paid to her in Court today, by means of a demand draft.
8.
Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, SI Shalini, P.S. Jafrabad.

9. A demand draft bearing no. 135337, dated 26.02.2024, for Rs. 2,00,000/- drawn on Canara Bank,
Govindpuram Colony, Ghaziabad, UP, has been handed over to the complainant/Respondent No.2,
who acknowledges the receipt of the same.

The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.
11. Learned APP for the State submits that investigation in the present FIR is pending and chargesheet is yet to be filed.
In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

12. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-

15. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
